sources.title: Holistic Agent Leaderboard
sources.observation: Cost-aware agent benchmarking and a reusable harness existed a year before this study. The authors describe 21,730 rollouts across nine benchmarks.
sources.scope: HAL datasets and configurations. Different pricing and cache conventions can affect comparisons.

sources.title: An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents
sources.observation: Four models were evaluated across 176 matched settings on SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2.1.
sources.scope: Component-level changes inside a controlled harness. This demonstrates older feasibility of matched comparisons.

sources.title: Pairing Matters
sources.observation: The study applies a common grader and metering setup to six harnesses and three lightweight coding models on 100 shared issues.
sources.scope: One observed trial for each issue and pairing. The 100 issues and controlled configurations define the population actually observed.

sources.title: Pairing Matters research artifact, version 1
sources.observation: The Figshare version and DataCite's Issued date agree on October 22. The GitHub companion appeared October 23. Its task-level table includes failures and common token accounting.
sources.scope: Charged tokens include repeated and cached context at full weight. Unreported usage is not imputed. Energy, accelerator occupancy, verification labor, billed cash and live client transfer are unmeasured.

sources.title: Beyond Leaderboard Ranks
sources.observation: The authors study budget-constrained selection from 58,197 HAL run-task records and compare successive halving and other allocation policies.
sources.scope: A direct competitor on agent selection, with cost and statistical uncertainty. Its data and pricing are distinct from the registered self-hosted cohort.

sources.title: Progress on provable inference for large language models
sources.observation: The authors demonstrate proofs of committed inference for a large mixture-of-experts model. Their verifier has lower hardware requirements than the prover.
sources.scope: Upstream demonstration. A local hash, benchmark verdict or copy of the paper is insufficient to authenticate a particular response.

sources.title: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5
sources.observation: The index introduced an evaluation covering 70 scientific terminal workflows alongside other benchmark changes.
sources.scope: A suite for testing agents on defined tasks. Real experimental discoveries and applicability to a beneficiary's workflow require independent evidence.

flagship_options.title: Select a self-hosted coding system that merits a pilot
flagship_options.before: A team could evaluate locally with an agent harness, or use the paired comparisons and HAL research available by October 13.
flagship_options.after: A publicly archived 18-way, task-matched matrix makes a budget-specific retrospective comparison on these 100 issues possible without commissioning those runs.
flagship_options.obstruction: Headline scores conceal the overlap between solved tasks and charges for unsuccessful attempts.
flagship_options.disposition: Construct the offline retrospective pilot selector.
flagship_options.economic_test: Have a team bring a representative private backlog, an independent acceptance oracle and measured hardware and staff costs; compare technical and complete-cost decisions.
flagship_options.alternative: A capable analyst with the same matrix and SQL. HAL and the budget-selection research provide broader existing methods.

flagship_options.title: Verify which model produced a computation
flagship_options.before: A customer could run a local trusted model, rely on provider attestations, or use prior proof systems within their supported model scope.
flagship_options.after: FlashProve extends a proof approach to a reported 400-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model.
flagship_options.obstruction: A response alone does not establish committed-model provenance. The input/output statement, model commitment, proof and compatible verifier must match.
flagship_options.disposition: Keep on watch for an actual independently verifiable customer receipt or a public proof set in scope.
flagship_options.economic_test: Measure recipient verification and issuer proof costs against running or trusting the incumbent under the same confidentiality requirement.
flagship_options.alternative: Use FlashProve's own verifier directly. Full local replay may suffice for a recipient with the model.

flagship_options.title: Qualify a research workflow for independent scientific replay
flagship_options.before: HAL, CORE-Bench and reproducible scripts supported computational replication before the window.
flagship_options.after: The October scientific terminal benchmark adds a set of independently scored workflows that can guide experiment selection.
flagship_options.obstruction: A benchmark pass may fail to transfer to an institution's actual scientific endpoint or validated instrument.
flagship_options.disposition: Defer a beneficiary-specific trial pending an authorized task, environment and reference measurement.
flagship_options.economic_test: Replay one eligible computational workflow against a conventional expert script and charge environment setup, checking and review.
flagship_options.alternative: Use the published Harbor task and verifier directly after task and license review.

offers.question: coding-pilot
offers.title: Adopt the highest observed resolution rate
offers.value: Quickly nominate a starting point for a self-hosted pilot.
offers.method: Read the authors' all-task summary table.
offers.tradeoff: Training and audit issues are pooled; the mean resource ceiling is unchecked.
offers.test: Compare the headline winner's audit issue scores and all-attempt tokens with the frozen allowance.

offers.question: coding-pilot
offers.title: Adopt an established cost-aware evaluator
offers.value: Reuse mature evaluation infrastructure for future local triage.
offers.method: Use the HAL evaluator and its existing public records.
offers.tradeoff: The public HAL cohort does not establish this exact 18-way grid. Cash and charged-token units differ.
offers.test: Match the requested systems, tasks, grader and accounting definitions before transporting a result.
offers.effort: Inspect task and configuration overlap before any new run.

offers.question: coding-pilot
offers.title: Remeasure all systems on a private backlog
offers.value: Measure fit to the actual institution, with its own grader.
offers.method: Run a prospectively metered factorial trial on approved machines and issues.
offers.tradeoff: Requires models, compute, data rights, independent grading and the cost of every attempted cell.
offers.test: Obtain permission, freeze task selection and record a complete pilot block before expansion.
offers.effort: One new model run per issue and selected configuration, plus independent grading.

offers.question: coding-pilot
offers.title: Target the failure mode worth repairing
offers.value: Find a targeted repair worth instrumenting on the next trial.
offers.method: Use the authors' reviewed failure categories to formulate a falsifiable intervention.
offers.tradeoff: Diagnosis does not measure repair efficacy or choose an affordable deployment configuration.
offers.test: Freeze a repair, run fresh issues and compare with unchanged harness behavior.
offers.effort: Review published categories first; a treatment effect needs new executions.

offers.question: coding-pilot
offers.title: Acquire just enough trials to choose a system
offers.value: Save evaluation effort when a full fresh matrix is expensive.
offers.method: Use the HAL-based study's allocation baselines, including successive halving.
offers.tradeoff: Prospective cost information and correctly priced, comparable trials matter. Its 48 shared SWE Mini issues differ from this cohort.
offers.test: Check performance with and without advance cell costs on new governed trials.
offers.effort: Reuse existing selection code or acquire additional samples under a registered budget.

offers.question: model-provenance
offers.title: Verify a committed inference receipt
offers.value: Determine whether a precisely identified computation matches the service commitment.
offers.method: Assemble a matching public statement, commitment, proof and compatible upstream verifier.
offers.tradeoff: No beneficiary proof, verified commitment or matching transcript accompanies this study.
offers.test: Pass an authentic receipt and reject a statement that differs from the committed one.
offers.effort: Inspect statement compatibility, then run the upstream verifier when the bundle exists.

offers.question: science-replay
offers.title: Replay a scientific workflow under an independent verifier
offers.value: Measure which research steps a terminal agent can actually complete.
offers.method: Freeze one appropriate public workload and its independent scientific criterion.
offers.tradeoff: A production scientific endpoint needs its own data rights, environment and acceptance.
offers.test: Run the same scientific endpoint with a competent conventional script.
offers.effort: Inspect one task's data rights, environment and verifier before executing.

transformations.title: Replay every pairing on the same withheld issues
transformations.value: Choose a configuration or pair under a resource allowance without buying another round of inference.
transformations.method: Partition issues once, choose on calibration rows, charge every recorded attempt, then evaluate the locked choice on audit issues.
transformations.tradeoff: Replay depends on the published grader and sample. A two-system portfolio requires an equivalent oracle to select a passing patch in practice.
transformations.test: Hold out issues, compare with an independent exhaustive SQL implementation and keep unfavourable outcomes.
transformations.effort: Read 1,800 licensed measurements and run a finite offline search. SQL can compute the same result.
